tips.title: Assembling Multi-Part Gun Barrels (Trumpeter, AFV Club)
tips.text: With Trumpeter and AFV Club kits, multi-part gun barrels can be a challenge. Dry-fit parts first. Apply Tamiya Extra Thin Cement to the mating surfaces, join parts, and apply light pressure with tweezers. After 30 seconds, dip the joint in water to stop curing. Once parts are separated, apply Vallejo Airbrush Thinner to remove excess cement. After curing, paint parts separately with Vallejo Model Color before assembly for easier cleanup.

tips.title: Using Jigs for Wing Alignment (Meng, ICM)
tips.text: For Meng and ICM kits with delicate wing assemblies, create a jig using foam board or plastic card. Mark wing root ribs on both fuselage halves and the jig. Assemble the wings on the jig, aligning rib marks. Glue with Tamiya Extra Thin Cement, applying light pressure. Once cured, remove the jig. For additional strength, apply super glue along the wing roots before joining.

tips.title: Installing Photo-Etch Parts (Eduard, Arma Hobby)
tips.text: For Eduard and Arma Hobby photo-etch parts, use a dedicated photo-etch bending tool to shape parts. Apply a small amount of Micro-Scale Liquid Decal Film Set on the backing sheet to prevent parts from falling off. Carefully bend parts, then soak in warm water for 30 seconds to remove any remaining film. Fit parts, using tweezers for fine adjustment. Attach with super glue or CA glue, allowing to cure before handling.

tips.title: Working with Resin Conversion Kits (Clear Prop Models)
tips.text: With Clear Prop Models resin kits, assemble main structures first, using CA glue. After 24 hours, clean up seams with a needle file or hobby knife. To strengthen thin parts, insert a small brass rod (0.3mm) into a drilled hole, applying CA glue. Once cured, cut excess rod. Prime with Vallejo Surface Primer before painting.

tips.title: Assembling Tracks (Individual Link vs Vinyl vs Workable)
tips.text: For individual link tracks, use CA glue, applying sparingly. Join links with tweezers, letting cure before handling. For vinyl tracks, soften with warm water, stretch around drive wheels, and allow to set. For workable tracks, apply Vallejo Plastic Putty to joins, letting dry before handling. Always dry-fit tracks before painting to ensure proper fit.
